rationale: Because RANK(·) is non-negative, this expression is the exact arithmetic negation of the archived FloatFinancedProfitability, so every statistic is already known by construction (alpha ≈ +4.4%, t ≈ +4.05, but fmb ≈ −0.30 against the stated positive sign) — it is a relabeled duplicate, not a new test.

A genuine decomposition that swaps the liquid-asset carrier for a short-maturity-obligation carrier with a hypothesis that matches the expression's direction, though it inherits the archive's repeatedly weak "centered distress × profitability rank" template and overlaps with the known debt-maturity/short-term-debt literature.

Internally consistent and motivated by the best-aligned prior signal, but it is a conditioning-state tweak rather than a new mechanism, and the claim that "coverage should be essentially unchanged since only che is added" is contradicted by the archive's only che-based signal (CashRunwayForWeakEarners), which failed at 0% coverage.

A pure horizon extension of the archive's strongest signal whose dominant leg — three-year liability growth scaled by assets — is close to the published asset/liability-growth (Cooper-Gulen-Schill) anomaly, so a confirming result would be hard to distinguish from that known effect.

Economically coherent and the most substantive change in the batch — it replaces accounting profit with an operating-cash-flow numerator in the obligation-coverage frame — with the honest caveat that oibdp − Δwcap is the classic Sloan accrual adjustment, so part of any result will be the accruals anomaly interacted with a standard cash-flow-to-total-debt credit ratio.

This is the same expression as LenderRateVersusReportedProfit (a 1% winsor changes almost nothing) with the expected sign simply relabeled to match the portfolio leg, which is post-hoc sign-fitting rather than a new test — and the fmb slope will remain roughly −0.57, i.e. against the newly stated positive sign.
